strongest_angle: Researchers at UT Austin and Sandia National Laboratories developed a green metathesis chemical recycling method that breaks down poly(dicyclopentadiene) thermoset composites to recover intact carbon and glass fibers without incineration.

key_facts.fact: Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin and Sandia National Laboratories created a metathesis-based recycling strategy for poly(dicyclopentadiene) thermoset plastics.
The chemical deconstruction method was developed across 4 academic and government institutions, including UIUC and MIT, to recover 2 types of intact fibers: glass and carbon fibers.
Lead author Keldy S. Mason and co-author Meghan T. Kiker published the metathesis-based deconstruction technique in a September 2026 Science Advances study.
In a laboratory test at The University of Texas at Austin, scientists deconstructed a 3D-printed pufferfish object made of pDCPD plastic using an eco-friendly solvent and ruthenium-based catalyst.

quotes.text: A 3D-printed pufferfish made of pDCPD undergoes deconstruction in a solution containing an eco-friendly solvent and ruthenium-based catalyst.
